title.en: Better to Reign in Hell: The Consult of Pandemonium
title.zh: 寧在地獄為王：萬魔殿的密議

region.zh: 萬魔殿，地獄議事堂（異象之境）

source.work: Paradise Lost, John Milton, books I-II

summary.en: The fallen host wakes on the burning lake; Satan rallies them with the epic's most quoted defiance — 'All is not lost—the unconquerable will... to wage by force or guile eternal war' — while Mammon's legions quarry the gold of Hell to raise Pandemonium. In council, Moloch calls for open war, Belial cringes, Mammon argues for Hell as a kingdom, and Beelzebub delivers Satan's own scheme: the new world of Man. The catalogue of fallen angels and the founding of the infernal commonwealth follow.
summary.zh: 墮落者在火湖上醒來；撒但以全詩最著名的抗辯召集他們——「尚未全失——那不屈的意志……以武力或詭計進行永恆的戰爭」——瑪門的兵團開採地獄之金築起萬魔殿。密議中，摩洛主戰，彼列怯懦，瑪門主張以地獄為國，別西卜代陳撒但之計：新造的人間世界。墮天使的名錄與地獄邦國的創立隨之鋪展。

sensitivity.note: Christian literary-religious imagination; the infernal parliament is Milton's epic invention, shaped by 17th-century politics.

passages.text: All is not lost—the unconquerable will, and study of revenge, immortal hate, and courage never to submit or yield: and what is else not to be overcome? That glory never shall his wrath or might extort from me. To bow and sue for grace with suppliant knee, and deify his power who, from the terror of this arm, so late doubted his empire—that were low indeed. Since, through experience of this great event, in arms not worse, in foresight much advanced, we may with more successful hope resolve to wage by force or guile eternal war, irreconcilable to our grand Foe, who now triumphs, and in th' excess of joy sole reigning holds the tyranny of Heaven. So spake th' apostate Angel, though in pain, vaunting aloud, but racked with deep despair.

There stood a hill not far, whose grisly top belched fire and rolling smoke; the rest entire shone with a glossy scurf—undoubted sign that in his womb was hid metallic ore, the work of sulphur. Thither, winged with speed, a numerous brigade hastened: as when bands of pioneers, with spade and pickaxe armed, forerun the royal camp, to trench a field, or cast a rampart. Mammon led them on—Mammon, the least erected Spirit that fell from Heaven; for even in Heaven his looks and thoughts were always downward bent, admiring more the riches of heaven's pavement, trodden gold, than aught divine or holy else enjoyed in vision beatific.

The Fiend looked up and knew his mounted scale aloft: nor more; but fled murmuring, and with him fled the shades of night. Meanwhile, Satan, on the burning lake, thus to his legions: Peace is despaired; for who can think submission? War, then, war open or understood, must be resolved. He spake; and, to confirm his words, outflew millions of flaming swords, drawn from the thighs of mighty Cherubim; the sudden blaze far round illumined Hell. Highly they raged against the Highest, and fierce with grasped arms clashed on their sounding shields the din of war, hurling defiance toward the vault of Heaven.

title.en: Sin and Death Build the Bridge over Chaos
title.zh: 罪與死在混沌之上築橋

region.en: Chaos, between Hell and the new world (vision-setting)
region.zh: 混沌，地獄與新世界之間（異象之境）

source.work: Paradise Lost, John Milton, book II

summary.en: Satan, himself the bridge, 'on the broad circumference hung on his shoulders like the moon' — wings like sails, beaming like a comet — threads the howling vagary of Chaos by sign and star. As he passes, Sin and Death, left behind in Hell, feel their works begin: the sovran of Hell builds his own road, a vast and long bridge 'wonderous to the sight' of ninefold gates and three-fold stairway, along which Sin and Death march to work the ruin the Fiend's rebellion will open. The bridge is the epic's cosmic geometry of Fall.
summary.zh: 撒但自身即是橋——「如滿月懸掛於肩後」——翅膀如帆，光芒如彗星，穿過混沌的呼號而前行。他一過，留在地獄的罪與死便覺其事業開始；地獄君王為自己築就長橋，奇觀巍然，而罪與死沿橋而行，去成就叛者所開啟的毀壞。這座橋是全詩墮落的宇宙幾何。

sensitivity.note: Christian literary-religious imagination; Sin-Death personifications are Milton's invention.

passages.text: He scarce had ceased when the superior Fiend was moving toward the shore; his ponderous shield, ethereal temper, massy, large, and round, behind him cast. The broad circumference hung on his shoulders like the moon, whose orb through optic glass the Tuscan artist views at evening from the top of Fesole, or in Valdarno, to descry new lands, rivers or mountains in her spotty globe. His spear, to equal which the tallest pine hewn on Norwegian hills, to be the mast of some great admiral, were but a wand, he walked with, to support uneasy steps over the burning marle, not like those steps on Heaven's azure; the hostile dread of his departure made them bow to the seas.

title.en: Eve Plucks the Fruit: Earth Felt the Wound
title.zh: 夏娃摘果：大地感到創傷

region.en: Tree in the midst of Eden

source.work: Paradise Lost, John Milton, book IX

summary.en: Milton's epic turns 'from truculent and satirick brawls' to tragedy: the serpent reasons Eve into the fruit — 'greedily she ingorged without restraint, and knew not eating death' — and 'Earth felt the wound; and Nature from her seat, sighing through all her works, gave signs of woe, that all was lost.' Adam's love-lament follows — 'How art thou lost!... flesh of flesh, bone of my bone thou art' — and he chooses to fall with her. The tradition's great retelling of the fall, set into the doctrine of original sin.
summary.zh: 史詩由刀劍與嘲諷轉入悲劇：蛇以言辭說動夏娃——「她貪婪地盡情吞嚥，不知吃下的乃是死亡」——「大地感到創傷；自然自其寶座，於萬物之中歎息，顯出哀兆：一切都失落了。」隨後是亞當的哀歌——「你怎麼失落了！……你是骨中之骨，肉中之肉」——他選擇與她同墮。這是原罪教義最偉大的重述。

sensitivity.note: Christian literary-religious imagination; the fall narrative retold for the doctrine of original sin.

passages.text: No more of talk where God or Angel guest with Man, as with his friend, familiar us'd, to sit indulgent, and with him partake rural repast; permitting him the while venial discourse unblam'd. I now must change those notes to tragick; foul distrust, and breach disloyal on the part of Man, revolt, and disobedience: on the part of Heaven now alienated, distance and distaste, anger and just rebuke, and judgement given, that brought into this world a world of woe, sin and her shadow Death, and Misery death's harbinger.

So saying, her rash hand in evil hour forth reaching to the fruit, she plucked, she eat! Earth felt the wound; and Nature from her seat, sighing through all her works, gave signs of woe, that all was lost. Back to the thicket slunk the guilty Serpent; and well might; for Eve, intent now wholly on her taste, nought else regarded; such delight till then, as seemed, in fruit she never tasted, whether true or fancied so, through expectation high of knowledge; not was Godhead from her thought. Greedily she ingorged without restraint, and knew not eating death.

O fairest of Creation, last and best of all God's works, Creature in whom excelled whatever can to sight or thought be formed, holy, divine, good, amiable, or sweet! How art thou lost! how on a sudden lost, defaced, deflowered, and now to death devote! Rather, how hast thou yielded to transgress the strict forbiddance, how to violate the sacred fruit forbidden! Some cursed fraud of enemy hath beguiled thee, yet unknown, and me with thee hath ruined; for with thee certain my resolution is to die: how can I live without thee! how forego thy sweet converse, and love so dearly joined, to live again in these wild woods forlorn!

title.en: The World Was All Before Them: Expulsion from Eden
title.zh: 全世界在他們面前：逐出伊甸

source.work: Paradise Lost, John Milton, book XII

summary.en: The archangel Michael leads the exiled pair up a mount of vision, shows them the history of the world to come, and girds their loins for exile — 'the world was all before them, where to choose their place of rest, and Providence their guide: they, hand in hand, with wandering steps and slow, through Eden took their solitary way.' The last eight lines of the epic made the homeless pair the West's emblem of mortality borne by providence.
summary.zh: 天使長米迦勒引被逐的二人登異象之山，展示未來世界史，並束其腰以備流亡——「全世界都在他們面前，可供選擇棲身之所，而天意是他們的嚮導：他們手牽著手，以緩慢的漫遊腳步，走過伊甸，踏上了他們孤寂的路。」史詩的最後八行，使這對無家夫婦成為西方「以天意承載必死之身」的象徵。

sensitivity.note: Christian literary-religious imagination; the exile close is among the most quoted endings in English poetry.

passages.text: The world was all before them, where to choose their place of rest, and Providence their guide: they, hand in hand, with wandering steps and slow, through Eden took their solitary way.

title.en: Paradise Regained: The Tempter Foiled in All His Wiles
title.zh: 復樂園：試探者詭計盡破

region.zh: 曠野與聖殿殿頂（異象之境）

source.work: Paradise Regained, John Milton, book I and IV

summary.en: Milton's brief epic answers Paradise Lost: 'I, who erewhile the happy Garden sung by one man's disobedience lost, now sing Recovered Paradise to all mankind, by one man's firm obedience fully tried through all temptation, and the Tempter foiled in all his wiles.' The Satan of the wilderness trial, once foiled, still returns 'as a swarm of flies in vintage-time'; at the temple's pinnacle he dares the leap; offered the world for one worship — 'the abominable terms, impious condition' — the Son answers with the first commandment, 'Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and only Him shalt serve.'
summary.zh: 彌爾頓的短史詩回應《失樂園》：「我先前歌詠因一人悖逆而失落的樂園，如今歌詠萬人重得的樂園——靠一人的堅定順服，受盡試煉，試探者詭計盡破、被擊退。」曠野受試的撒但屢敗屢返，「如釀酒季的蒼蠅群」；於殿頂之上他竟敢誘其一躍；以萬國榮華換一拜——「可憎的條款，不虔的條件」——聖子以第一誡作答：「當拜主你的神，單要事奉祂。」

sensitivity.note: Christian literary-religious imagination; the inversion of the fall by obedience is Milton's theological structure.

passages.text: I, who erewhile the happy Garden sung by one man's disobedience lost, now sing Recovered Paradise to all mankind, by one man's firm obedience fully tried through all temptation, and the Tempter foiled in all his wiles, defeated and repulsed, and Eden raised in the waste Wilderness. Now had the great Proclaimer, with a voice more awful than the sound of trumpet, cried Repentance, and Heaven's kingdom nigh at hand to all baptized. To his great baptism flocked with awe the regions round, and with them came from Nazareth the son of Joseph deemed to the flood Jordan—came as then obscure, unmarked, unknown.

Whom thus our Saviour answered with disdain:— I never liked thy talk, thy offers less; now both abhor, since thou hast dared to utter the abominable terms, impious condition. But I endure the time, till which expired thou hast permission on me. It is written, the first of all commandments, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and only Him shalt serve. And dar'st thou to the Son of God propound to worship thee, accursed? now more accursed for this attempt, bolder than that on Eve, and more blasphemous; which expect to rue. The kingdoms of the world to thee were given! Permitted rather, and by thee usurped.

So Satan, whom repulse upon repulse met ever, and to shameful silence brought, yet gives not o'er, though desperate of success, and his vain importunity pursues. Or as a swarm of flies in vintage-time, about the wine-press where sweet must is poured, beat off, returns as oft with humming sound; or surging waves against a solid rock, though all to shivers dashed, the assault renew, vain battery! and in froth or bubbles end.
